claims.note: Secondary source: Search Engine Roundtable quotes the email Google sent to advertisers (the Google help page does not give the date). Verify the quote typography against the page.

claims.question: Q2

claims.note: Law firms or legal services are not named in this exception on this page.

claims.question: Q3

claims.quote: Caller will hear: ‘Google and its partners may record or return all calls for quality and research purposes, subject to our privacy policies. This call is not confidential.’ Recipient (law firm) will hear: ‘Call from Google. This call is recorded and may not be attorney-client privileged.’
claims.note: Describes the whisper wording as of 2020-2021, as relayed to the bar by Google through a marketing vendor; Google's current help pages do not print this wording, so confirm the live wording by test call.

claims.question: Q3

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The State Bar of Wisconsin's ethics counsel wrote that, absent informed consent from prospective clients, a lawyer who authorizes Google to record and disclose LSA calls and texts violates the confidentiality duty.
claims.quote: Consequently, unless the prospective clients give informed consent, the lawyer violates the duty of confidentiality by authorizing Google to access, monitor and record phone calls and text messages, and by authorizing Google to disclose information to third parties.
claims.note: Wisconsin Inside Track article by Aviva Meridian Kaiser, ethics counsel. It is a bar staff article, not a formal ethics opinion. No withdrawal or update found. It concerns Local Services Ads as of 2020-2021, before the 2025 terms.

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The Wisconsin article said Google's whisper message does not give a layperson adequate information on the material risks of recording, so it does not supply informed consent.
claims.quote: The “whisper message” does not communicate adequate information and explanation about the material risks of authorizing Google to access, monitor and record phone calls and text messages.

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The article said that having intake staff take basic details on the recorded line and call back on a private line still discloses client identity and information without informed consent.
claims.quote: While following this advice may minimize the amount of information disclosed, client identity and other information is disclosed and recorded without the client’s informed consent in violation of SCR 20:1.6.

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The article said whether participation is consistent with confidentiality depends on whether the person contacting the lawyer through the ad is a prospective client.
claims.quote: Whether a lawyer’s participation in the LSA is consistent with the lawyer’s duty of confidentiality depends whether the person contacting the lawyer through the LSA is a prospective client.

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The North Carolina State Bar ethics committee published Proposed 2021 FEO 5, which concluded that a lawyer's participation in a pay-per-lead program that records and retains communications was prejudicial to the administration of justice.
claims.quote: Proposed 2021 FEO 5 concluded that the structure of the advertising program renders a lawyer’s participation in it prejudicial to the administration of justice in violation of Rule 8.4(d)
claims.note: Article by Suzanne Lever in the NC State Bar Journal 27,2 (Summer 2022). The proposal did not become an opinion. The program is a Google Local Services Ads-type program per the article title. The proposed opinion text itself could not be fetched.

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: North Carolina's Ethics Committee withdrew Proposed 2021 FEO 5 at its April 2022 meeting.
claims.quote: at its meeting in April 2022, the Ethics Committee withdrew Proposed 2021 FEO 5.
claims.note: Status: withdrawn; no formal NC opinion on this program exists.

claims.question: Q8
claims.claim: The committee said it concluded the recordings are not uniquely vulnerable to harmful third-party disclosure and that a platform-specific opinion would not benefit the profession or consumers.
claims.quote: the recordings at issue are not uniquely vulnerable to harmful third-party disclosures, and that adopting a specific ethics opinion related to this particular advertising platform would not benefit the legal profession or the consumers of legal services

claims.question: Q8

claims.question: Q8

claims.quote: Because you called us by clicking on an advertisement, the advertising company is able to record this call and anything you say will not be confidential. But if you will give me your phone number, I will be happy to call you back on a private line.

claims.note: Blog post in The Tech Savvy Lawyer, not a forum thread. No Reddit, Google Ads Community or lawyer-forum thread could be opened; see not_found.
